Fe, Co, and Mn K-edge XAS spectra of the samples were acquired on a laboratory high-throughput X-ray absorption fine structure spectrometer (Anhui Absorption Spectroscopy Instrument Co., Ltd., China) at the Tianjin University large-scale instrument platform in transmission geometry, with the corresponding metal foils measured in the same session for energy calibration. Larch25 was used for background removal, Fourier transformation, and fitting. The background radius Rbkg was 1.0 Å (1.3 Å for the MnO reference). The k2-weighted data were transformed with a Hanning window (dk = 1 Å−1). Fe and Co fits used k = 2.5–11.5 Å−1 and R = 1.0–3.2 Å, and Mn fits used k = 2.0–6.0 Å−1 and R = 1.0–3.0 Å. The FT spectra are not phase-corrected. Morlet wavelet transforms used η = 10 and σ = 1.26

Calculations were carried out on the supercomputing system of the Institute for Materials Research (IMR), Tohoku University, Japan, and Genkai at Kyushu University, Japan. VASP 6.6.0 with PAW-PBE and D3(BJ) dispersion was used. Reference numbers in this section follow the main-text bibliography. Relaxation energies and higher-precision electronic-analysis energies are kept separate.

Models and structural constraints. The supported models use the same orthorhombic 22.198 × 21.360 × 24.000 Å3 cell and a Γ-centered 1 × 1 × 1 k-point mesh. Their clean compositions are C174N4Fe27Co32Mn, C180Fe27Co32, and C174N4Mn. Each particle-containing model fixes 15 interior particle atoms, and all atoms of Mn–NC are free. The relaxed surface states under reaction conditions (8O* + Mn–OH* for FeCoMn–NC, 8O* for FeCo–NC, and Mn=O for Mn–NC) contain 248, 247, and 180 atoms, respectively. Their c-axis empty spans are approximately 12.59, 12.62, and 21.81 Å, calculated as the cell height minus the atomic z span. The fixed atoms (1-based indices) are 183, 189, 191, 192, 193, 195, 201, 213, 214, 217, 218, 225, 226, 229 and 230 in FeCoMn–NC and 185, 191, 193, 194, 195, 197, 203, 215, 216, 219, 220, 227, 228, 231 and 232 in FeCo–NC. They carry the fixed selective-dynamics flags in the deposited structure files (Data Availability Statement in the main text). The 59-atom particle represents a local particle–support environment.

Geometry optimization. PAW-PBE calculations used a 500 eV cutoff, D3(BJ) dispersion (IVDW = 12), ISPIN = 2, PREC = Normal, ALGO = Fast, EDIFF = 10−5 eV, EDIFFG = −0.02 eV Å−1, IBRION = 2, POTIM = 0.1, ISIF = 2, ISYM = 0, and LREAL = Auto. Gaussian smearing used SIGMA = 0.05 eV. The standard PAW datasets were C, N, Fe, Co, Mnpv, O, and H as required by composition, and Mn semicore p states were included. Initial moments were Fe/Mn 3, Co 2, O 0.5, and C/N/H 0 μB. Spin mixing used AMIX/BMIX = 0.1/0.0001 and AMIX_MAG/BMIX_MAG = 0.4/0.0001 with LMAXMIX = 4. A structure was accepted from the ionic-convergence marker and normal termination, and the final σ → 0 energy was used.

Electronic-structure and charge analysis. Fixed-geometry calculations used ENCUT = 500 eV, EDIFF = 10−6 eV, PREC = Accurate, LREAL = False, ALGO = Normal, ISMEAR = 0, SIGMA = 0.05 eV, IVDW = 12, LMAXMIX = 4, LORBIT = 11, NEDOS = 2000, LAECHG = True, and Γ-point sampling. The realized fine charge-density grid was 252 × 240 × 360.

FeCo(110) model. The adsorption calculations used ENCUT = 500 eV, PREC = Normal, EDIFF = 10−5 eV, EDIFFG = −0.02 eV Å−1, NSW = 300, IBRION = 2, POTIM = 0.2, ISIF = 2, ISYM = 0, LREAL = False, ALGO = Normal, NELM = 200, ISMEAR = 0, SIGMA = 0.10 eV, ISPIN = 2, LMAXMIX = 4 and IVDW = 12. Initial Fe/Co/O moments were 3/2/0.5 μB, and hydrogen initial moments were zero. LDIPOL = True and IDIPOL = 3 apply the dipole correction normal to the slab. DIPOL follows the slab/adsorbate center used in each input (z = 0.5310 for 6O and 0.5392 for 8O in fractional coordinates). Spin-mixing parameters were AMIX = 0.1, BMIX = 0.0001, AMIX_MAG = 0.4 and BMIX_MAG = 0.0001. LWAVE and LCHARG were False.

E denotes the final converged VASP energy (σ → 0). Gas references G(H2) and G(H2O) already include their gas-phase corrections. The adsorbate corrections given in Section 2.5 are added to the energy of each adsorbed state. Temperature is 298.15 K, e is the positive elementary charge, and U is an electrode potential.
2.5 Gas-reference sets and adsorbate corrections

Gas references and adsorbate corrections. The coverage curves and Table S10 retain the original coverage-library references G(H2) = −6.834 eV and G(H2O) = −14.341 eV. The ORR free energies in Table S7 use the unified references G(H2) = −6.833 eV and G(H2O) = −14.327 eV. Total adsorbate corrections ΔZPE − TΔS are +0.066 eV (O*), +0.343 eV (OH*), +0.403 eV (OOH*), and +0.210 eV (H* in the coverage library). The O*, OH* and OOH* values follow Table S1 of the Supporting Information to main-text ref. 12. The H* value is the coverage-library correction.
The last equation fixes the O2 reference through the equilibrium four-electron water-formation free energy. All adsorption energy differences use the matched relaxation energies in Table S11.

NM = 59, and the maximum metal displacement is max|δri|. Pair distances use minimum images. The coordination-count analysis uses a 3.0 Å metal–metal cutoff (self pairs excluded). Mn–N means are taken over the four retained N atoms.
